title: Build a closed-loop bioreactor controller
summary: A six-month build: vessel, sensors, firmware, and a tuned PID loop that holds dissolved oxygen + pH stable through a 72-hour continuous run.
realWorldDeliverableMd:
## What you ship

A working closed-loop fermentation rig with PID-tuned dissolved oxygen and pH control, demonstrated by a 72-hour continuous run. The deliverable is the integrated system, not any single piece — vessel, sensors, pumps, controller, firmware, and the data trace that proves it ran.

**Hardware:** Stirred-tank vessel (1-5 L), agitator drive, dissolved-oxygen + pH probes, peristaltic pumps for acid/base/feed, controller PCB with sensor amplifiers and MOSFET drivers.

**Firmware:** PID loop on a microcontroller (Arduino / RP2040 / ESP32 — your choice). Safety interlocks for overtemperature, foam-out, sensor disconnect.

**Bio:** Media prep, organism handling, sample prep for OD600 + offline validation.

**Validation receipts:** 72-hour continuous run with OD600 trace, vessel pressure log, dissolved-oxygen + pH logs at ≥1Hz, post-run cell viability check against a commercial reference culture. Writeup defending tuning choices and noting where the rig deviated from textbook PID behavior.

**Why AI alone can't do this:** Textbook PID gains aren't your system's gains — your vessel volume, agitator efficiency, sensor lag, and pump dynamics are the load-bearing knobs. The tuning loop is the student's. AI is hugely useful for circuit review, code review, datasheet extraction, derivation help — but the empirical loop is what matters.
contentUndergrad:
## Why this capstone

Most people who claim to know controls have only ever simulated systems they could solve analytically. A real bioreactor pushes back against you: sensors drift, pumps overshoot, organisms metabolize unevenly, and your textbook PID gains are wrong on day one.

This is a year-scale project precisely *because* you can't shortcut the empirical work. AI will write 80% of your firmware and review every PCB schematic you commit, but the tuning loop is yours. Same for the bio side — AI will tell you about *Pichia pastoris* growth dynamics in general, but it doesn't know your vessel's mixing time, your probe's response curve, or how your media batches actually behave.

## Scope of the build

You're shipping an integrated rig, not a CAD file or a writeup. The rubric scores the system end-to-end: did it run for 72 hours, did the controller hold setpoints, did the post-run validation match expectations, and does your writeup explain *why* the tuning landed where it did.

## How AI fits in

Use AI heavily. Ask it to derive the transfer function from your vessel geometry. Have it review every commit. Pair-program the firmware. Ask it to explain why your DO probe is reading wrong (then verify in the lab). The grader doesn't care how much AI you used — it cares whether you shipped a working rig and can defend the choices.

What AI can't do: run your hardware, validate against your media batch, pull a sample and check OD600 on the bench. The capstone is the iteration loop AI can't sit inside.

milestones.title: M1 — System spec + block diagram
milestones.description: Document the rig you're building: target organism, working volume, setpoint envelope (DO%, pH, temperature), and the control / safety interlocks. Includes a block diagram of all sensors, actuators, and signal paths, plus a parts BOM with budget. Defend choices in the writeup — why this organism, why this volume, why these probes.

criteria.description: Rig scope is achievable in 6 months and clears the year-scale floor.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the proposed rig is concrete + achievable + non-trivial across mechE/EE/bio/controls.

criteria.description: Block diagram is unambiguous about signal paths + interlocks.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score the block diagram for completeness — every sensor wired to a reader, every actuator wired to a driver, every safety check declared.

criteria.description: Choices are defended in the writeup.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the writeup actually defends the organism / volume / probe choices instead of treating them as defaults.

milestones.title: M2 — Vessel + agitator built and bench-tested
milestones.description: Vessel fabricated (machined or off-the-shelf modified), agitator installed, ports drilled for probes + pumps. Bench test: hold water at temperature, agitate at design RPM, no leaks under positive pressure for 1h.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether photos + bench-test data demonstrate a working vessel + agitator.
Score whether the CAD/drawings would let another builder reproduce the vessel.

milestones.title: M3 — Sensor + actuator integration + bench validation
milestones.description: Probes wired in, pumps mounted, controller PCB assembled. Sensor readings trended for ≥4 hours against known-water reference; pumps calibrated for actual mL/s vs commanded. Surface mismatches in the writeup.

criteria.description: Sensor data is logged + trends are reasonable.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether logged sensor data shows physically plausible behavior with known references.
Score the pump-calibration table + writeup.

criteria.description: Surfaces and discusses mismatches between expected and actual.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the learner identified things that didn't behave as expected and discussed why.

milestones.title: M4 — PID firmware skeleton + closed-loop bench test (water)
milestones.description: PID loop running on the controller, holding a synthetic setpoint (e.g. heater PWM controlling water temperature) within ±2% of setpoint for ≥30 minutes. Includes a tuning-log writeup showing how Kp/Ki/Kd landed where they did.

criteria.description: Loop holds setpoint to ±2% over the test window.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score the closed-loop performance from logs.

criteria.description: Tuning log shows iteration, not blind copy-paste.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the tuning log demonstrates real iteration vs textbook gains pasted in.
Score firmware code quality + structure.

milestones.title: M5 — First organism run + dissolved-oxygen control
milestones.description: Inoculate the rig with a model organism (E. coli, S. cerevisiae, or P. pastoris). Hold dissolved oxygen at setpoint through exponential growth. Likely fails the first 1-2 attempts — that's expected. Writeup must explain failure modes and corrections.

criteria.description: First successful run with DO held at setpoint through exponential.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether logs show DO control held during a real organism's exponential phase.
Score the writeup's diagnosis of earlier failed runs.

criteria.description: pH is monitored even if not yet under closed-loop control.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score pH logging + any mitigation discussion.

milestones.title: M6 — Full closed-loop control: DO + pH
milestones.description: Both DO and pH under closed-loop control simultaneously. Demonstrate setpoint changes — e.g. raise DO from 30% to 60% mid-run — and show the controller responds without windup or oscillation.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score the dual-loop performance from logs.
Score the step-response data.

criteria.description: Anti-windup or saturation handling is documented.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether anti-windup is implemented + discussed.

milestones.title: M7 — 72-hour continuous run
milestones.description: The capstone test: a 72-hour continuous fermentation run with both control loops active throughout. Log everything at ≥1Hz. Pull samples at intervals for offline OD600 + viability checks. Some unanticipated event WILL happen — document it.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the 72-hour run completed with continuous logging.
Score control quality across the run, including any documented perturbations.

criteria.description: Offline samples corroborate the online story.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score offline OD600 + viability data against the online trace.
Score the writeup's account of anything weird that happened.

milestones.title: M8 — Validation, writeup, and defense
milestones.description: Compare end-state of the 72-hour run against a commercial reference culture or published expectation. Write the full project report — including limitations, what you'd build differently, and what AI couldn't do for you. This is the artifact the world sees.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score the validation against reference — does the comparison address known sources of difference?

criteria.description: Writeup demonstrates the iteration the project required.
criteria.aiPrompt: Score the depth of the writeup — does it actually explain the 6-month arc?
Score the limitations section — does it identify real gaps vs trivial ones?
Score the section discussing what AI couldn't do — was it honest?
